summary: Tower the FFLA marks gone at Fisher Peak, on the Carroll County and Surry NC line; the Piedmont Land Conservancy describes the peak and its preserve but not a tower.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone. No source describes what remains at the site.

evidence.supports: FFLA Virginia list: Fisher Peak, tower, gone, at 36.56005, -80.82324
evidence.quote: Fisher Peak Carroll / Surrey (NC) 36.56005 -80.82324 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: FFLA county page files Fisher Peak under Carroll with Surrey (NC) written beside it, tower gone
evidence.quote: Carroll / Surrey (NC) Fisher Peak 36.56005 -80.82324 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Conservancy: the peak is in the northwest corner of Surry County where the Blue Ridge Parkway reaches the NC/VA line
evidence.quote: the northwest corner of Surry County where the Blue Ridge Parkway reaches the North Carolina/Virginia state line

evidence.supports: Conservancy: the peak rises to nearly 3,300 feet
evidence.quote: Fishers Peak rises to nearly 3,300 feet

evidence.supports: Conservancy: has protected more than 1,800 acres of the area
evidence.quote: PLC has protected more than 1,800 acres of this significant natural area

evidence.supports: Conservancy: the property is completely forested

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA spells the peak Fisher Peak and the conservancy spells it Fishers Peak. The conservancy's peak is probably the same mountain, since both name the same peak on the same state line; the record keeps the FFLA name.
The FFLA writes Surrey (NC) and the conservancy writes Surry County for the same North Carolina county. The FFLA spelling looks like a misspelling; the story uses Surry.

notes_for_editor: Two sources give the tower only as gone; the conservancy page describes the peak and preserve, not a tower, so the identity of its peak with the FFLA point is inferred from name and the state line. No source gives a build date, builder, design, height, agency, staffing, fire history or access. A search result pointed to a Facebook group post recalling a new fire tower on Fisher's Peak Mountain around 1948; that page was not readable from the cache, so it is not used. A mapcarta search snippet gives a different elevation (3,533 ft) from the conservancy's nearly 3,300 feet; not fetched, not used.
